checksum_mismatch.pattern: (?i)change ?sets? check ?sum.*(?:was:.*but is now:|is now different)|checksum.*(?:was:.*but is now:|is now different|changed|does not match)
checksum_mismatch.message:
⚠️ CHANGESET MODIFICATION DETECTED

❌ Problem:
You modified an already executed changeset. The SQL body was changed after it was already run on the database.

✅ Solution:
1. Revert your changes to the original changeset
2. OR create a NEW changeset with a different ID for your modifications
3. OR delete the changeset entry from DATABASECHANGELOG table (only in dev/test)
4. OR use liquibase clearCheckSums command (not recommended)

Example:
--liquibase formatted sql
--changeset author@company.co:new_changeset_id_v2 stripComments:false
-- This is the NEW changeset with your modifications
CREATE TABLE...

Note:
Never modify executed changesets in production. Always create new changesets for changes.

duplicate_changeset.message:
⚠️ DUPLICATE CHANGESET ID

❌ Problem:
This changeset ID already exists in the database.

✅ Solution:
Change the changeset ID to a unique value.

Example:
--changeset author@company.co:table_name_action_timestamp

missing_table.message:
⚠️ MISSING TABLE/RELATION

❌ Problem:
The SQL references a table that doesn't exist yet.

✅ Solution:
1. Check if the table name is spelled correctly
2. Ensure the table is created in an earlier changeset
3. Check the schema name is correct

DROP EXISTING FUNCTION.message:
⚠️ MISSING: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS

❌ Problem:
Your function does not have 'DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS' statement before CREATE.

✅ Solution:
Add this line before your CREATE FUNCTION statement:

Example:
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS schema_name.function_name(argument_types);
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION schema_name.function_name(...)

DROP EXISTING PROCEDURE.message:
⚠️ MISSING: DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS

❌ Problem:
Your procedure does not have 'DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS' statement before CREATE.

✅ Solution:
Add this line before your CREATE PROCEDURE statement:

Example:
DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS schema_name.procedure_name(argument_types);
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE schema_name.procedure_name(...)

DROP EXISTING VIEW.message:
⚠️ MISSING: DROP VIEW IF EXISTS

❌ Problem:
Your view does not have 'DROP VIEW IF EXISTS' statement before CREATE.

✅ Solution:
Add this line before your CREATE VIEW statement:

Example:
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS schema_name.view_name;
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW schema_name.view_name AS ...

LB ENABLE.message:
⚠️ MISSING: Liquibase Header

❌ Problem:
This SQL file is missing the Liquibase formatted SQL header.

✅ Solution:
Add this as the FIRST line of your SQL file:

Example:
--liquibase formatted sql
--changeset author@company.co:changeset_id runOnChange:true stripComments:false splitStatements:false

LB CHANGESET.message:
⚠️ MISSING: Changeset Metadata

❌ Problem:
This SQL file is missing the changeset line.

✅ Solution:
Add the changeset line after the liquibase header:

Example:
--liquibase formatted sql
--changeset your.email@company.co:unique_changeset_id runOnChange:true stripComments:false splitStatements:false

LB STRIP_COMMENTS.message:
⚠️ MISSING: stripComments:false

❌ Problem:
Your changeset is missing 'stripComments:false' attribute.

✅ Solution:
Add 'stripComments:false' to your changeset line:

Example:
--changeset author@company.co:id runOnChange:true stripComments:false splitStatements:false

LB STRIP_STMT.message:
⚠️ MISSING: splitStatements:false

❌ Problem:
Your changeset is missing 'splitStatements:false' attribute.

✅ Solution:
Add 'splitStatements:false' to your changeset line:

Example:
--changeset author@company.co:id runOnChange:true stripComments:false splitStatements:false

LB RUN_ON_CHANGE.message:
⚠️ MISSING: runOnChange:true

❌ Problem:
Your procedure/function/view is missing 'runOnChange:true' attribute.

✅ Solution:
Add 'runOnChange:true' to your changeset line:

Example:
--changeset author@company.co:id runOnChange:true stripComments:false splitStatements:false

Note:
This is REQUIRED for all procedures, functions, and views to update when code changes.

MISSING_PRIMARY_KEY.message:
⚠️ MISSING: Primary Key

❌ Problem:
This table in the 'global' schema does not have a PRIMARY KEY defined.

✅ Solution:
Add a PRIMARY KEY constraint to your table:

Example:
CREATE TABLE global.product_master (
    product_id integer NOT NULL,
    product_name text,
    PRIMARY KEY (product_id)
);

Note:
All tables in 'global' schema MUST have a primary key for data integrity.

EMOJI_IN_SQL.message:
⚠️ INVALID: Emoji Characters Detected in SQL

❌ Problem:
Your SQL file contains emoji characters which can cause:
• Database encoding issues (UTF-8 vs UTF-16)
• Replication failures across different systems
• Query execution errors
• Migration problems between environments
• Compatibility issues with older database versions

✅ Solution:
1. Remove all emoji characters from your SQL file
2. Use plain text descriptions instead of emojis
3. If you need special characters, use standard ASCII symbols
4. Replace emojis with descriptive words

Example:
BAD:  CREATE TABLE orders (status varchar); -- 📦 ✅ ❌
GOOD: CREATE TABLE orders (status varchar); -- Package, Success, Error

BAD:  COMMENT ON COLUMN users.name IS 'User name 👤';
GOOD: COMMENT ON COLUMN users.name IS 'User name (person)';

Note:
Emojis are not standard SQL and can cause serious production issues. Use plain text only.

MISSING_UNIQUE_INDEX.message:
⚠️ MISSING: Unique Index on Materialized View

❌ Problem:
This materialized view in 'inventory_smart' schema does not have a UNIQUE INDEX.

✅ Solution:
Add a UNIQUE INDEX after your materialized view creation:

Example:
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW inventory_smart.ph_master AS ...;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_ph_master_unique ON inventory_smart.ph_master (product_id, store_id);

Note:
Unique indexes on materialized views are required for refresh concurrency.

CASCADE.message:
⚠️ DANGEROUS: CASCADE Operation Detected

❌ Problem:
Using CASCADE can automatically drop dependent objects without explicit control, which may lead to unintended data loss.

✅ Solution:
1. Remove the CASCADE keyword from your DROP statement
2. Manually drop dependent objects in the correct order
3. If CASCADE is absolutely necessary, add this file to exceptions.json

Example:
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS dependent_view;
DROP TABLE schema_name.table_name;

Note:
CASCADE operations are blocked to prevent accidental deletion of dependent objects.

LOCK.message:
⚠️ DANGEROUS: LOCK Statement Detected

❌ Problem:
LOCK statements can cause performance issues and deadlocks.

✅ Solution:
1. Remove the LOCK statement from your SQL
2. If LOCK is absolutely necessary, add this file to exceptions.json

Example:
LOCK TABLE schema_name.table_name IN EXCLUSIVE MODE;

Note:
LOCK statements are blocked to prevent performance issues and deadlocks.

DROP TABLE.message:
⚠️ DANGEROUS: DROP TABLE Statement Detected

❌ Problem:
DROP TABLE statements can cause permanent data loss in production databases.

✅ Solution:
1. For views, use DROP VIEW instead of DROP TABLE
2. If you need to recreate a table, use ALTER TABLE to modify it instead
3. For temporary refactoring, add this file to exceptions.json after review
4. Ensure you have proper backups before dropping tables

Example:
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS schema_name.view_name;
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW schema_name.view_name AS ...

Note:
DROP TABLE is blocked to prevent accidental data loss. Contact db-architects@impactanalytics.co for exceptions.

DROP TRIGGER.message:
⚠️ WARNING: DROP TRIGGER Statement

❌ Problem:
Dropping triggers can break automated workflows and data integrity checks.

✅ Solution:
If the trigger needs to be replaced, use:
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trigger_name ON schema_name.table_name;
CREATE TRIGGER trigger_name ...

DROP CONSTRAINT.message:
⚠️ WARNING: DROP CONSTRAINT Statement

❌ Problem:
Dropping constraints can compromise data integrity.

✅ Solution:
Ensure the constraint is being replaced or is no longer needed.
ALTER TABLE schema_name.table_name DROP CONSTRAINT constraint_name;
ALTER TABLE schema_name.table_name ADD CONSTRAINT new_constraint ...

DROP COLUMN.message:
⚠️ DANGEROUS: DROP COLUMN Statement

❌ Problem:
Dropping columns causes permanent data loss.

✅ Solution:
1. Verify the column is no longer used by any queries or applications
2. Consider archiving the data first
3. Get approval from db-architects@impactanalytics.co

TRUNCATE.message:
⚠️ DANGEROUS: TRUNCATE Statement

❌ Problem:
TRUNCATE removes all rows from a table and cannot be rolled back easily.

✅ Solution:
1. For procedures starting with 'sync_', this may be allowed
2. Otherwise, use DELETE with WHERE clauses for more control
3. Add to exceptions.json if required for data refresh operations

GRANT.message:
⚠️ SECURITY: GRANT Statement Detected

❌ Problem:
GRANT statements modify database permissions and should be managed centrally.

✅ Solution:
Contact DevOps or db-architects@impactanalytics.co for permission changes.

REVOKE.message:
⚠️ SECURITY: REVOKE Statement Detected

❌ Problem:
REVOKE statements modify database permissions and should be managed centrally.

✅ Solution:
Contact DevOps or db-architects@impactanalytics.co for permission changes.

ONLY.message:
⚠️ WARNING: ONLY Keyword Detected

❌ Problem:
The ONLY keyword can cause unexpected behavior with table inheritance.

✅ Solution:
Review if ONLY is necessary for your use case or remove it.

DROP PROCEDURE.message:
⚠️ WARNING: DROP PROCEDURE Statement

❌ Problem:
Dropping procedures can break application functionality.

✅ Solution:
This should typically be in exceptions.json for procedures.
Ensure the procedure is being replaced with CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE.

DROP FUNCTION.message:
⚠️ WARNING: DROP FUNCTION Statement

❌ Problem:
Dropping functions can break application functionality.

✅ Solution:
This should typically be in exceptions.json for functions.
Ensure the function is being replaced with CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION.
